hero.title: No Waste Mate
paragraphs: NoWasteMate is a capstone thesis project developed collaboratively by a three-person team, where I led key aspects of the user experience and core application architecture.
While the project was built as a team, my role focused on shaping the system architecture and the overall user experience, ensuring the app was intuitive, cohesive, and well-structured as it grew.

concepts.label: KEY CONCEPTS LEARNED
items: Designing scalable client–server architectures with clear separation of concerns.
Button placement and navigation depth impact how quickly users complete daily tasks.
Figma iteration turned abstract ideas into testable interface flows.
Enforced Jira usage clarified ownership and prevented missed work.
Centralized Confluence documentation reduced review and handoff friction.
Firebase Authentication secured user access and database operations.
Token-based authentication validated client requests to backend services.
Swagger streamlined API testing and endpoint validation.
A layered Python API structure supported scalable development.

body.title: Design Development & Process
paragraphs: Over the course of a three-month semester, I worked closely with my group members to shape the logo and overall design language for NoWasteMate. Design has always been something I naturally gravitate toward, and I had the most hands-on experience with Figma, which allowed me to take the lead in turning early ideas into tangible visuals.

Before working in Figma, I spent several years using Adobe Photoshop and Illustrator, and that background strongly influenced how I approached layout, colour, and visual consistency throughout the project.

One of my main focuses during the design process was creating an experience that felt accessible and effortless to use. Since users are expected to log their food items on a daily basis, it was important to minimize the number of steps required and to automate details wherever possible.

body.title: Implementation & Engineering
paragraphs: From a technical perspective, I focused heavily on structuring the backend in a way that would remain maintainable as features expanded. The FastAPI service was organized into routes, services, and models to support modular development.
I implemented Firebase Authentication to handle user accounts and secure access to Firestore data. Token-based authentication was used to validate client requests and protect sensitive operations.
Swagger was used throughout development to test endpoints and verify request–response contracts, ensuring that the mobile client and backend remained in sync.
